origin.usage: stri_locate_all_regex(str, pattern, omit_no_match = FALSE, capture_groups = FALSE, get_length = FALSE, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If TRUE, drop the row for a string that does not match.

arguments.name: capture_groups
arguments.text: If TRUE, attach the start and end of each capture group.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: If TRUE, the second column is the match length.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. A zero-length match has end equal to start minus 1. get_length reports length instead of end, and a miss is -1, -1. A missing string stays NA, NA. capture_groups attaches one matrix per parenthesized group. Group names are kept when the pattern is a single pattern. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. Each string is a matrix. A miss is one NA row, or -1, -1 when get_length is TRUE. omit_no_match drops that row.

translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_locate_all_regex
